items.title: Why mutation testing doesn't run on every commit
items.description: Every mutant means rerunning the whole test suite once more — total run time is mutants generated times the suite's own runtime. Drag the number of mutants a module generates (a larger, more complex module generates more) to see how fast that adds up, holding the suite's own runtime fixed at its current slider value.

params.name: suiteRunSeconds
params.label: Time for one full test-suite run

items.compute: const totalMinutes = Math.round((params.numMutants * params.suiteRunSeconds / 60) * 10) / 10; return { totalMinutes };

items.title: How boundary-test coverage moves the mutation score
items.description: In L3's shipping-fee example, the suite already killed the two non-boundary mutants (the arithmetic and statement-removal ones) without any extra work — those two are 'free.' The other two mutants are both conditional-boundary mutants, and each is only killed once a test sits exactly on its threshold. Drag the slider to see the mutation score move as boundary-exact tests get added, from the original suite's 0% boundary coverage (score: 50%, exactly matching L3's worked example) up to full boundary coverage (score: 100%).

params.name: boundaryCoveragePercent
params.label: Fraction of boundary mutants killed by an exact-threshold test

items.compute: const totalMutants = 4; const nonBoundaryKilled = 2; const boundaryMutants = totalMutants - nonBoundaryKilled; const boundaryKilled = boundaryMutants * (params.boundaryCoveragePercent / 100); const mutationScore = Math.round(((nonBoundaryKilled + boundaryKilled) / totalMutants) * 1000) / 10; return { mutationScore };
